title: Mathematics
subtitle: Textbook for Class VIII
_direction: tile, its own direction: comb’s type arrangement (a dark front, the spine going with it) in wine, amber and cream, so the two parts of Class 8 read as a pair. The artwork is this volume’s own proof that two squares make one: the same four right triangles in two equal squares, leaving a² and b² one way and c² the other, with a² + b² = c² beneath (Chapters 2, 4 and 7). It replaced a copy of arc’s discs and floating figures, which were Class 9’s and said nothing about this book. The back is this cover’s own (back.html): the series’ Class 8 words over a straight edge of right triangles, with square markers, instead of arc’s curve. None of its colours is on another subject’s wrap: the back’s lede, which was a burnt orange close to Science’s, is now a wine rose. No finish is declared: on a direction the finish is inert.
